Rendering: How About That New Fiat Punto?
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | kdesignag
Chances are you do not care about the Fiat Punto if you live in the United States of America, but Europeans may want to pay attention to this model, as rumor has it that it might return from the dead.
Unofficial information speaks about a possible introduction at the end of 2027 or in 2028, though it has yet to be confirmed at this point. Such a thing could utilize Stellantis’ CMP/e-CMP construction, and this means that both internal combustion lumps and electric powertrains could be in the pipeline.
A brand-new Fiat Punto based on that platform would mean that the model would share its nuts and bolts with the Fiat 600, as well as the Citroen C4, DS 3 Crossback, Opel / Vauxhall Corsa, Mokka, Peugeot 208, 2008, and other similar models, including the Jeep Avenger. The Alfa Romeo Junior and the Lancia Ypsilon are also based on this construction.
Mind you, we haven’t kept the latter two for last for nothing, because some of their styling cues have inspired the model pictured in the gallery. This is nothing more than a mere rendering take on a hypothetical new-gen Fiat Punto, and for what it’s worth, nothing suggests that the actual car will look anything like this CGI project. But then again, a new Punto hasn’t been officially confirmed, as we already told you.
Photo: Instagram | kdesignag Signed by @kdesignag and shared on social media recently, this imagined new Fiat Punto looks more like a subcompact crossover than a traditional supermini. It has the company’s name on the grille, which is flanked by a pair of T-shaped headlights the remind us of certain Volvos, as well as extra DRLs on the sides of the bumper. T-shaped taillights can be seen at the rear, alongside a bumper that’s similar to the front one.
There is black plastic cladding on the lower parts of the body, including on the wheel arches, and these, as well as the generous ground clearance, as well as the car’s overall proportions, make it look more like a crossover. And that’s probably for the best, as traditional passenger cars, including subcompact hatchbacks, have lost traction to high-riding models.
As a reminder, Fiat made three generations of the Punto . The last one saw the light of day between 2004 and 2018 in Europe, and it was assembled not only in Italy, but also in India and Brazil. Giorgetto Giugiaro at Italdesign was responsible for sketching it out.
The model was offered as a hatch and a panel van, with a front-engine and front-wheel drive layout, and was based on the same construction as the era’s Linea, Fiorino, Alfa Romeo MiTo, and Opel Corsa (D). The powertrain family comprised numerous gasoline engines, as well as a CNG, and a few diesel units, and it varied from one market to the other.
